attribution.note: Marcus's own blog post, stating his view and quoting his own email to Newton. Endorsed first-person claim.

semantics.note: Firm 'will' language: AGI will come, not soon, and new ideas will be needed because the pursued hypothesis was basically disproven. The proposition matches this and adds nothing. No calendar horizon is given.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary. It does not substitute LLM scaling for the unnamed hypothesis or invent a deadline for 'not soon'. It correctly says that non-arrival cannot disprove an open-ended forecast.

evidence.note: Levels of AGI framework (v5, Sept 2025). Gives one possible way to measure AGI. Marcus did not adopt it, and it says nothing about whether AGI has arrived.

AGI Society, Sept 2026: the published evidence does not yet support saying GPT-6 Astra is AGI. So the Huang and Brockman declarations are not a verified arrival. This neither proves nor disproves the forecast.
ARC Prize, Sept 2026: Astra made major ARC-AGI-3 progress, but the report cautions this is not proof of AGI. It does not identify Marcus's hypothesis or test whether new ideas were needed.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. Nothing in the packet shows a verified AGI arrival by 2026-10-28: the Astra declarations are disputed (e2), and ARC Prize cautions that its benchmark progress is not proof of AGI (e3). No evidence settles the timing, the unnamed hypothesis, or whether new ideas were needed. Non-arrival cannot settle an open-ended forecast, so it stays unresolved.
